newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU WEAKER VS DLR ON STALLED MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU WEAKER VS DLR ON STALLED MARKET.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Tuesday lower with dealers' quotes ranging from 7,500/600 to 8,000/100 to the dollarr but interbank trading remained stalled amid low hard currency offer, traders said.
They hailed the central bank (BNR) move to restore local dealer licences to 24 banks, which now act as market makers along with the existing four dealers.
But they said the move to liberalise the market could not solve the long-standing hard currency squeezes as dollar holders were still waiting for fresh lows.
"Some of my clients are willing to pay as much as 8,500 for the greenback," said one trader.
"I see the leu quoted down, near 8,500/9,000 in the days ahead," said another.

Most operators said the 9,000 level might be a resistance point for the dollar, but few of them ventured to anticipate a longer term trend for the leu, which sagged by some 95 percent since January 1.
Short-term rates jumped to 140 percent from 130 percent with the money market struggling to cope with leu shortages, traders said.

Some dealers said the BNR might take advantage of the cash- starving money market to supply the much-craved leu funds through interventions to buy dollars rather than to offer more refinancing at weekly auctions.
"Players are chasing for leu funds to meet their minimum reserve targets as penalties for reserve shortages are now pretty high," said one trader.
Penalties for unmet reserves equal the BNR's Lombard rate which now stands at an annual 200.72 percent.
Leu-dollar retail prices were at 7,800/8,200, somewhat lower than 7,700/8,000 in the morning.
